subcommands.name: put-metric-alarm
subcommands.description: Creates or updates an alarm and associates it with the specified metric, metric math expression, anomaly detection model, or Metrics Insights query.

options.name: --alarm-name
options.description: The name for the alarm. This name must be unique within the Region. The name must contain only UTF-8 characters, and can't contain ASCII control characters

options.name: --alarm-description
options.description: The description for the alarm

options.name: --actions-enabled
options.description: Indicates whether actions should be executed during any changes to the alarm state. The default is TRUE

options.name: --no-actions-enabled
options.description: Indicates whether actions should be executed during any changes to the alarm state. The default is TRUE

options.name: --ok-actions
options.description: The actions to execute when this alarm transitions to an OK state from any other state. Each action is specified as an Amazon Resource Name (ARN).

options.name: --alarm-actions
options.description: The actions to execute when this alarm transitions to the ALARM state from any other state. Each action is specified as an Amazon Resource Name (ARN).

options.name: --insufficient-data-actions
options.description: The actions to execute when this alarm transitions to the INSUFFICIENT_DATA state from any other state.

options.name: --metric-name
options.description: The name for the metric associated with the alarm. For each PutMetricAlarm operation, you must specify either MetricName or a Metrics array.

options.name: --namespace
options.description: The namespace for the metric associated specified in MetricName

options.name: --statistic
options.description: The statistic for the metric specified in MetricName, other than percentile. For percentile statistics, use ExtendedStatistic.

options.name: --extended-statistic
options.description: The extended statistic for the metric specified in MetricName.

options.name: --dimensions
options.description: The dimensions for the metric specified in MetricName

options.name: --period
options.description: The length, in seconds, used each time the metric specified in MetricName is evaluated. Valid values are 10, 30, and any multiple of 60.

options.name: --unit
options.description: The unit of measure for the statistic. For example, the units for the Amazon EC2 NetworkIn metric are Bytes because NetworkIn tracks the number of bytes that an…

options.name: --evaluation-periods
options.description: The number of periods over which data is compared to the specified threshold.

options.name: --datapoints-to-alarm
options.description: The number of data points that must be breaching to trigger the alarm. This is used only if you are setting an "M out of N" alarm.

options.name: --threshold
options.description: The value against which the specified statistic is compared.

options.name: --comparison-operator
options.description: The arithmetic operation to use when comparing the specified statistic and threshold. The specified statistic value is used as the first operand.

options.name: --treat-missing-data
options.description: Sets how this alarm is to handle missing data points. If TreatMissingData is omitted, the default behavior of missing is used.

options.name: --evaluate-low-sample-count-percentile
options.description: Used only for alarms based on percentiles.

options.name: --metrics
options.description: An array of MetricDataQuery structures that enable you to create an alarm based on the result of a metric math expression.

options.name: --tags
options.description: A list of key-value pairs to associate with the alarm. You can associate as many as 50 tags with an alarm.

options.name: --threshold-metric-id
options.description: If this is an alarm based on an anomaly detection model, make this value match the ID of the ANOMALY_DETECTION_BAND function.

options.name: --cli-input-json
options.description: Performs service operation based on the JSON string provided. The JSON string follows the format provided by ``--generate-cli-skeleton``.

subcommands.name: put-metric-data
subcommands.description: Publishes metric data to Amazon CloudWatch. CloudWatch associates the data with the specified metric.

options.name: --namespace
options.description: The namespace for the metric data. You can use ASCII characters for the namespace, except for control characters which are not supported.

options.name: --metric-data
options.description: The data for the metrics. Use this parameter if your metrics do not contain associated entities. The array can include no more than 1000 metrics per call.

options.name: --entity-metric-data
options.description: Data for metrics that contain associated entity information.

options.name: --strict-entity-validation
options.description: Whether to accept valid metric data when an invalid entity is sent.

options.name: --no-strict-entity-validation
options.description: Whether to accept valid metric data when an invalid entity is sent.

options.name: --metric-name
options.description: The name of the metric

options.name: --timestamp
options.description: The time stamp used for the metric.  If not specified, the default value is set to the time the metric data was received

options.name: --unit
options.description: The unit of metric

options.name: --value
options.description: The value for the metric.  Although the --value parameter accepts numbers of type Double, Amazon CloudWatch truncates values with very large exponents.

options.name: --dimensions
options.description: The --dimensions argument further expands on the identity of a metric using a Name=Value pair, separated by commas, for example: --dimensions InstanceID=1-23456…

options.name: --statistic-values
options.description: A set of statistical values describing the metric

options.name: --storage-resolution
options.description: Valid values are 1 and 60. Setting this to 1 specifies this metric as a high-resolution metric, so that CloudWatch stores the metric with sub-minute resolution…

subcommands.name: put-metric-stream
subcommands.description: Creates or updates a metric stream. Metric streams can automatically stream CloudWatch metrics to Amazon Web Services destinations, including Amazon S3, and to…

options.name: --name
options.description: If you are creating a new metric stream, this is the name for the new stream.

options.name: --include-filters
options.description: If you specify this parameter, the stream sends only the metrics from the metric namespaces that you specify here.

options.name: --exclude-filters
options.description: If you specify this parameter, the stream sends metrics from all metric namespaces except for the namespaces that you specify here.

options.name: --firehose-arn
options.description: The ARN of the Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to use for this metric stream.

options.name: --role-arn
options.description: The ARN of an IAM role that this metric stream will use to access Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose resources.

options.name: --output-format
options.description: The output format for the stream. Valid values are json, opentelemetry1.0, and opentelemetry0.7.

options.name: --tags
options.description: A list of key-value pairs to associate with the metric stream. You can associate as many as 50 tags with a metric stream.

options.name: --statistics-configurations
options.description: By default, a metric stream always sends the MAX, MIN, SUM, and SAMPLECOUNT statistics for each metric that is streamed.

options.name: --include-linked-accounts-metrics
options.description: If you are creating a metric stream in a monitoring account, specify true to include metrics from source accounts in the metric stream

options.name: --no-include-linked-accounts-metrics
options.description: If you are creating a metric stream in a monitoring account, specify true to include metrics from source accounts in the metric stream
